## 1. Motivation and Background

Proportion data arise in many scientific settings.  Examples 1, 2, 3 etc.  Traditionally this type of data has modeled using normal regressions techniques with transformations of the response variable such as the the arcsin square root transformation.  However, this method is known to be flawed.  Some have even referred to it as "asinine".  Other alternatives include using logistic/ binomial regression, however, these require the statistical practitioner to know the denominator (i.e. the $n$ of these proportions).  In many settings all we have is the proportion.  In these cases, a better alternative is beta regression (CITATION).  Beta regression is well studied (IS IT?) with established packages available in R. @Kosmidis2026
